original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Exact one-point partial form of the length-22 pair identity: for every n=7 weight split with parts at most 11 that survives B0+a*b>=need, the maximum pair product after adding one missing parity-legal point is at least need. The strict one-point prune therefore deletes no branch of those splits.
scope_change_reason: The card's first experiment, reconstructing 01021323, is already recorded in open PRs #3821 and #3699. This package takes the next uncovered census-pruning obligation from the length-22 handoff: a monotone partial form of the pair identity in MATH.md section 3. The delivered statement is a sharp non-pruning theorem for that one-point form, not another enumeration.
bottleneck_link: A corrected length-22 exclusion would pin f(7) to {22,24} in the PR943 word model. This does not decide that exclusion. It shows one proposed partial pair-identity prune cannot delete a branch on any basic-identity survivor, so engine work should not be spent on the coset-wide one-point test.
stop_rule: Stop once the one-point floor is proved for every basic-identity survivor and the (9,9) equality witness is recomputed. Do not run a length-22 census.
evidence: verify.py recomputes every n=7 basic-identity survivor (3820 rows, parts at most 64), checks h(S_min) >= need, checks the ceil-drop lemma for M=2..64, rebuilds the (9,9) witness with outside f identically 5, and checks the f-sum identities on every subset pair in F_2^3 and F_2^4. test_verify.py repeats the (9,9) and (7,11) arithmetic with literals and shows that the floor swap drops (7,11) from 7 to 6.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance (Cursor Grok), including the averaging argument, the verifier, and overlap checks. No independent human or formal-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Does restricting the same one-point maximum to the n hypercube neighbors of the current prefix vertex strictly prune any open length-22 split?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The coset-wide maximum proved here is at least the walk-legal maximum. A neighbor restriction could still fall below need even though the coset-wide test never does.
open_questions.first_step: On one open split, evaluate S+f(p) only at the neighbors of each vertex of an explicit partial prefix set whose coset-wide ceiling equals need.
open_questions.blocked_by: Legal extensions are walk steps, not arbitrary coset points. This package does not search walks.

open_questions.question: Does an exact two-point completion ceiling strictly prune the (9,9) split?
open_questions.why_it_matters: One point before the leaf is the strongest exact window that still never prunes. Two points is the next place a partial pair test could delete branches.
open_questions.first_step: Minimize, or lower-bound, the maximum of S+f(p)+f(r)+A_{p xor r} over odd pairs outside an 7-point odd set paired with a 9-point even set.
open_questions.blocked_by: A greedy sample reached 17, above need 9. That sample is not a lower bound.
